tables.title: Internal input/output signals
tables.text: Table 238, "Internal input/output signals", in section 30.3.2 (PKA internal signals) on page 917. Columns: Signal name, Signal type, Description. 3 data row(s). Notes: 1. When tamper is active, the AHB interface is blocked: RAM and register reads are 0-ed and writes are ignored. There is no PKA RAM erase.

rows: Public key accelerator IP global interrupt request

PKA internal tamper event signal to TAMP (XOR-ed), 
triggered when an unexpected fault occurs while PKA 
manipulates secrets, or when the programmed input point is 
not found on the input curve (ECDSA signature and ECC 
scalar multiplication only). A tamper is also generated if 
application does not respect the maximum supported size of 
operands, or when PKA finds a fault in critical configuration 
(1)registers.
This signal is asserted as soon as a fault is detected. When 
asserted, read access to PKA registers are reset to 0 and 
writes are ignored.
The signal is de-asserted when PKA memory is cleared.
notes: 1. When tamper is active, the AHB interface is blocked: RAM and register reads are 0-ed and writes are ignored. There is no PKA RAM erase.
